research.job_description_summary: Infosys hires freshers (BE/B.Tech/ME/M.Tech/MCA/MSc, 2024-2026 batches, 60% or 6.0 CGPA, no active backlogs) as Systems Engineer, Specialist Programmer and Digital Specialist Engineer. Secondary sources describe an online test (aptitude, reasoning, pseudocode, and DSA coding for Specialist Programmer; Automata Fix for Digital Specialist Engineer), a technical interview (programming, DBMS, OS, project) and an HR interview. Training is at the Mysuru campus.
limitations: The official Infosys pages that could be fetched (infosys.com careers and graduates pages, last modified 2026-05-05) name programmes such as HackWithInfy, InfyTQ and Power Programmers but list no fresher roles, rounds or eligibility; the role and process description comes from a secondary aggregator (freshershunt.in, 2026-06-23), which also says the drive had closed.

The largest candidate-reported source is an anonymous aggregate on freshershunt.in (published 2026-08-19, 220 questions, 1,097 citations). Counts are user-submitted estimates; some entries are garbled, and several listed questions show no count (recorded as at least one report).
placementpreparation.io content is labelled 'sample questions' and is not attributed to candidates; it was used only as topic context.
No question reports specific to Specialist Programmer or Digital Specialist Engineer were found; those tracks use original practice questions (class D) mapped to the described focus areas.
The 2026 aptitude, pseudocode and debugging items are original practice items, not reported questions.
Package figures differ between sources and were not used.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a Docker container and a virtual machine?
questions.relevance_to_role: A secondary source describes Specialist Programmer as advanced coding, full-stack and DevOps with a DSA-based online test; the Infosys graduate page names HackWithInfy and Power Programmers.
questions.expected_answer: Containers share the host kernel and package only the app and its dependencies, so they are lighter and start faster. Virtual machines run a full guest OS on a hypervisor, giving stronger isolation but more overhead.
follow_ups: When would you prefer a VM?
questions.notes: Topic area comes from a secondary description of the Infosys process; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://freshershunt.in/infosys-system-engineer-specialist-2026/.

questions.prompt: How would you design a REST API for a to-do application? Cover URLs, HTTP methods, status codes and idempotency.
questions.relevance_to_role: A secondary source describes Specialist Programmer as advanced coding, full-stack and DevOps with a DSA-based online test; the Infosys graduate page names HackWithInfy and Power Programmers.
questions.expected_answer: Resources like /tasks and /tasks/{id}; GET list/read, POST create (201), PUT or PATCH update, DELETE (204). GET, PUT and DELETE are idempotent; POST is not. Use 400 for bad input, 404 for missing, 401/403 for auth, pagination for lists.

questions.prompt: What is a race condition? Show how two threads incrementing a shared counter can go wrong and how to fix it.
questions.relevance_to_role: A secondary source describes Specialist Programmer as advanced coding, full-stack and DevOps with a DSA-based online test; the Infosys graduate page names HackWithInfy and Power Programmers.
questions.expected_answer: Increment is read-modify-write, so two threads can read the same value and lose an update. Fix with a mutex or synchronized block, or an atomic increment.
questions.notes: Topic area comes from a secondary description of the Infosys process; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://freshershunt.in/infosys-system-engineer-specialist-2026/.

questions.prompt: How does a database index speed up queries, and what does it cost?
questions.relevance_to_role: A secondary source describes Specialist Programmer as advanced coding, full-stack and DevOps with a DSA-based online test; the Infosys graduate page names HackWithInfy and Power Programmers.
questions.expected_answer: A B-tree index lets lookups and range scans avoid reading the whole table. It costs extra storage and slows writes because the index must be updated; choose indexes for selective, frequently filtered or joined columns.
follow_ups: Why might the optimizer ignore an index?
questions.notes: Topic area comes from a secondary description of the Infosys process; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://freshershunt.in/infosys-system-engineer-specialist-2026/.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between git merge and git rebase, and when should you avoid rebase?
questions.relevance_to_role: A secondary source describes Specialist Programmer as advanced coding, full-stack and DevOps with a DSA-based online test; the Infosys graduate page names HackWithInfy and Power Programmers.
questions.expected_answer: Merge combines histories with a merge commit and preserves them; rebase replays commits on top of another branch for a linear history but rewrites commits. Avoid rebasing branches others have already pulled.
follow_ups: How do you resolve a merge conflict?
